junk_imagery.evidence: The illustrations match the story: a chargeback form on a laptop (mid1), printed evidence photos (mid2), and the seller celebrating in a furniture showroom (mid4). They are generic but on-topic.

decorative_mascot.evidence: No mascot appears in any frame from hook@0.3 to payoff@-0.4. Channel separation is correct.

bare_number_card.evidence: No number card appears. The only numbers are the 45.2k/6.1k counts on the post card (hook@0.3).

dead_air.evidence: The gameplay keeps moving in every frame (measured longest_static_s 0.0). But the top illustration stays the same from mid2 to mid3 (~10s) and from mid4 to payoff@-0.4 (~12s).

empty_void.evidence: Both halves fill the frame in every sample. No large dark areas (dark_fraction 0.0).

unreadable.evidence: The post card title (hook@0.3) and the captions (mid1 'NEVER RECEIVED IT.', mid4 'NORMAL RETURN UNDER') are large, high-contrast and clear of other marks.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: No frame shows the chair or the public marketplace listing, which is the story's twist and its title. The evidence-desk image (mid2, mid3) has a truck photo and store CCTV stills while the caption says 'SAME GARAGE SHOWN'. The seller-celebration image then stays up from mid4 through payoff@-0.4 for ~12s.
weakest_scene.root_cause: Illustrations were picked at a generic level ('person at desk with evidence', 'person happy at computer') instead of from the beat's own content. As a result, the reveal moment, the listing, never gets its own picture. Each image is held across several beats.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Give seg3 its own illustration of a phone or browser marketplace listing showing the same $1,200 leather chair in a garage. Make the seg4 evidence image show that listing screenshot beside loading-dock footage. Change the top image at least every ~6s so no single still carries the last 12s.

depictions.note: A chargeback form on a laptop fits the action. The person shown is a woman while the story's buyer is 'he', and nothing shows the 'never received' lie.
A generic evidence desk. A truck photo and CCTV stills stand in for 'vehicle plate'. The caption says 'same garage shown' but no garage or listing is visible.
The seller fist-pumps at a green checkmark, which reads as winning. It is a generic stock-style image and stays up for the last ~12s.

grades.one_line: The premise and the post-card hook are strong, but the twist (the chair in his own marketplace listing) is never shown. Generic illustrations are held 10-12s each, so the reveal doesn't land.
problems: The chair and the marketplace listing, the story's title and twist, never appear in any sampled frame.
The evidence-desk image (mid2-mid3) shows a truck and store CCTV while the caption says 'SAME GARAGE SHOWN'. Picture and narration don't match.
The same celebration image is held from mid4 (43s) to the end (55s). The top half is visually stale for the payoff.
mid1 shows a woman filing the chargeback in a story about a man.
The ending caption 'A REMARKABLY CROWDED' trails off. The payoff line is not visually landed.
fixes: Add a dedicated illustration for seg3: a marketplace listing screenshot showing the same leather chair, timed to the reveal line.
Rebuild the seg4 evidence image around the listing screenshot, the loading-dock video still and the plate, so it matches the caption.
Change the top illustration at least every ~6s. Split the final 12s into 'bank denies chargeback' (a denial notice) and the closing beat.
Match the buyer's gender in the illustrations to the story ('he').
